profiles.purpose: The single visual language for MPS Pilates flashcards, quote cards, and movement sheets.

visualLanguage.medium: hand-drawn ink and pencil gesture illustration
visualLanguage.linework: imperfect organic lines, varied pressure, visible dry-brush texture
visualLanguage.anatomy: elongated expressive gesture with believable joints and readable contact points
visualLanguage.facialDetail: few ink marks; preserve glasses, hair silhouette, and profile identity
visualLanguage.lighting: white paper with sparse charcoal shadow blocks
visualLanguage.mood: quiet, poetic, intimate, reflective, lightly humorous

composition.subjectScale: one dominant gesture with generous negative space
composition.apparatus: thin hand-drawn geometry; simplify only after preserving contact and load direction
composition.text: no text in artwork; optional quote text belongs in a separate quote-card layer

lockedCharacterRules: Use the approved or currently reviewed teacher-01 character reference.
Preserve the shoulder-length layered bob and round dark glasses.
Preserve the teacher's real body proportions; elongation is a gesture style, not a body redesign.
Current outfit: off-white thin-strap cropped Pilates camisole and dark charcoal high-waisted mid-thigh biker shorts.
Add a subtle natural dusty-rose pink tint to both cheeks; keep it soft and integrated with the ink and pencil linework.
Use the current canonical character sheet version recorded in the manifest.
Do not import a style reference person's face, hair, clothing, or body proportions.

panelTemplates.description: seated side gesture with quiet negative space
single-leg balance or long-line standing gesture
clean side profile with readable hair and glasses
one Mat movement drawn with clear body landmarks
Reformer pose with thin apparatus lines and preserved contact
Cadillac pose with spare bars, straps, and expressive line

reviewChecklist: Does the image read as hand-drawn rather than vector or photorealistic?
Are the lines imperfect but intentional?
Does the same teacher identity remain recognizable?
Does the exact MPS outfit remain unchanged?
Is the pink cheek tint subtle, symmetrical, and consistent without turning the artwork into a full-color style?
Is there generous white negative space?
Are contact points and apparatus lines still understandable?
